claims.text: Return the LanguageSpec for a path by extension, or None if unsupported.
claims.why: The function calls SPECS.get(Path(path).suffix.lower()) which returns LanguageSpec or None.

claims.text: A DocumentSpec is NOT a LanguageSpec and ``.md`` is deliberately NOT added to ``SPECS``.
claims.why: SPECS is built from _SPECS which does not include .md; .md is only in _DOC_SPECS.

claims.text: ``spec_for`` is not a lookup table, it is a CLAIM, and thirteen call sites read it as one:
claims.why: The list of call sites (index._collect, provider_router._looks_like_missed_source, etc.) is not present in this chunk.

claims.text: Every one of those reads is CORRECT about a document: prose has no functions, no imports and no clone units.
claims.why: The behavior of those call sites is not visible in this chunk.

claims.text: So the honest move is to leave ``spec_for`` answering None for documents -- it keeps its meaning, and all thirteen call sites keep theirs -- and to give documents their own registry that only the document path consults.
claims.why: spec_for returns None for .md (since .md is not in SPECS); doc_spec_for is provided for documents.

claims.text: Independent of ``spec_for``: a path answers non-None to exactly one of them (or to neither). Nothing answers both.
claims.why: SPECS and DOC_SPECS are built from disjoint extension sets; spec_for and doc_spec_for each check their respective dicts, so a path can match at most one.

claims.text: Return the DocumentSpec for a path by extension, or None.
claims.why: The function calls DOC_SPECS.get(Path(path).suffix.lower()) which returns DocumentSpec or None.

observations.what: Comment block lists 13 call sites that read spec_for as a lookup table; these are not in this chunk, so the claim is uncheckable.
The comment claims that .md is deliberately not in SPECS; this is confirmed by the code (no .md in _SPECS).
doc_spec_for returns None for paths not in DOC_SPECS; spec_for returns None for paths not in SPECS; the two registries are disjoint.
